workstream: Wave 3C-2c3 — Older DES public-park alias and status resolution
scope: Research/alias/status resolution only. No Civic Map asset additions, removals, renames or coordinate edits in this step.
methodology: Use the 2010 DES inventory as the historical baseline.
Prefer later Makati procurement/operations records to establish continuity.
Use current public map/business evidence to identify present names and geometry, but not to override official ownership/status evidence.
Merge historical/current names only when name, location and continuity evidence converge; otherwise preserve separate records.

sources.publisher: City Government of Makati — Department of Environmental Services

sources.role: Later named public-park inventory and locations.
Operational maintenance continuity for Buendia Plaza, Ayala Freedom Park and EDSA-Buendia Park.
Government reporting that Makati/MMDA inaugurated EDSA-Buendia Park and EDSA-Pinagkaisahan Park in 2023.

evidenceChain: 2010 DES inventory lists Buendia Plaza.
2020 Makati inventory replaces the name in the comparable public-park set with 'Gil Puyat - SLEX' at Mayapis Street, Barangay San Antonio.
2022 Makati APP again budgets recurring maintenance under the name Buendia Plaza.
Current map geometry identifies Buendia Plaza on Mayapis Street with City Government of Makati as operator.

currentMapEvidence.note: Current map barangay label resolves to Palanan. The 2020 city table labels the Mayapis site San Antonio; retain this historical/current barangay discrepancy for exact boundary review rather than rewriting the source.

aliasDecision.Buendia Plaza ↔ Gil Puyat - SLEX: high-confidence same-site continuity, but Makati did not publish an explicit alias statement in the reviewed documents.

evidenceChain: 2010 DES inventory lists Freedom Park.
2022 Makati APP budgets recurring maintenance for Ayala Freedom Park.
Current park listings identify Buendia Freedom Park on Sen. Gil J. Puyat/Ayala Avenue Extension and use the Makati City website/contact.

currentMapEvidence.address: Ayala Avenue Extension / Sen. Gil J. Puyat Avenue, Makati City

aliasDecision.Ayala Freedom Park → Buendia Freedom Par: probable current-name continuity based on current site identity/location; no reviewed Makati document explicitly publishes the rename.

evidenceChain: 2010 DES inventory lists EDSA Buendia Park.
2022 Makati APP budgets recurring maintenance for Edsa-Buendia Park.
Makati and MMDA inaugurated the improved EDSA-Buendia Park in February 2023; the park was designed by Makati DES and turned over to the local government.

currentMapEvidence.note: Current government reporting confirms the site at EDSA-Buendia, but this research pass did not identify a sufficiently precise distinct park geometry to freeze a Civic Map point.

evidenceChain: 2010 DES inventory separately lists Guadalupe Nuevo Linear Park.
Current map geometry identifies multiple contiguous Guadalupe Linear Park segments on J.P. Rizal Street adjacent to Guadalupe Nuevo Cloverleaf Park, operated by City of Makati.
The current geometry/location is consistent with the 2010 Guadalupe Nuevo linear-park identity and remains distinct from the cloverleaf park.

currentMapEvidence.note: The present park is linear/multi-segment; implementation should avoid pretending the whole park is represented by one arbitrary point if segment geometry can be supported.

parks.ownershipManagement: City of Makati / MMDA for the 2023 EDSA-Pinagkaisahan improvement
evidenceChain: 2010 DES inventory lists Pinagkaisahan Underpass Park.
2020 Makati inventory separately lists Kalayaan Avenue Park (Pinagkaisahan).
Makati and MMDA inaugurated EDSA-Pinagkaisahan Park in 2023, designed by Makati DES.
A current public park listing identifies Pinagkaisahan Park on Kalayaan Avenue.
parks.requiredAction: Use a Makati project plan, site plan, procurement description or official map to determine whether these names represent one evolving park, adjacent parks, or distinct assets.

evidenceChain: 2010 DES inventory lists Makati DES Linear Park at 3,672 sq m.
The reviewed later Makati named inventories and 2022 maintenance list do not identify a direct successor under this name.
The 2010 inventory separately lists Guadalupe Nuevo Linear Park and Valenzuela Linear Park, so this record cannot safely be collapsed into either one.

currentMapEvidence.note: No sufficiently reliable current site/name successor was found in this batch.

parks.requiredAction: Search later DES/DEPW project lists, old park maps/site plans and procurement descriptions for a location or rename.

implicationsForEarlierBatches.action: Treat as the 2020 naming/location phase of the Buendia Plaza record rather than a separate future Civic Map asset, subject to preserving the source-era name in provenance.
Keep on hold together with Pinagkaisahan Underpass Park until the lineage with EDSA-Pinagkaisahan Park is resolved.

findings: Buendia Plaza is a surviving public park and the evidence strongly supports continuity with the 2020 Gil Puyat-SLEX entry at the same Mayapis corridor.
Freedom Park has a credible present identity as Buendia Freedom Park, with Ayala Freedom Park as the documented 2022 intermediate name.
EDSA-Buendia Park is unquestionably current after the 2023 Makati/MMDA reinauguration.
Guadalupe Nuevo Linear Park survives as Guadalupe Linear Park and remains distinct from the Guadalupe Nuevo Cloverleaf Park.
Pinagkaisahan has a real current park lineage, but the names cannot yet be collapsed safely.
Makati DES Linear Park remains unresolved and blocks a fully closed historical-name audit.

nextStep.title: Close public-park verification research
nextStep.scope: Resolve remaining held/current-status cases across batches 1–3, prioritize Post Office Pocket Park, Makati City Hall Park, Playground Park Poblacion, Pinagkaisahan lineage and Makati DES Linear Park; then freeze the implementation set. No Civic Map changes.
